evidence: NOT WHEAT, AND NO WHEAT TO SUBSTITUTE (data_errors.csv iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin). The raw IIA extract has ZERO wheat production or area rows -- `wheat` there is trade only (imports 2,733, exports 2,024, reexports 229) -- and carries `spelt` (329 area + 323 production) and `meslin` (499 area + 490 production) instead, products layer B has no item for. Value-matched on (year, value, area/production), the 77 dated rows read 38 spelt and 14 meslin uniquely, the rest ambiguous and none wheat; the 176 period rows cannot be keyed by year. The split is per cell (czech republic 55% meslin), so no single relabel or factor recovers either crop, and the correct iia wheat series is EMPTY, not small. Published under FAO item 15 it sat beside juan/mitchell wheat on 68 (polity, wheat, unit, year) keys at a median 100x below them (28x-4,416x), and the consumer's mean over those keys was 51,314,316 against 101,316,950 from the other sources alone (wheat halved); once #451's resolver replaced the mean, all 68 keys were withheld as contradictions instead. With this rule they publish juan's wheat. state/item_equivalences.csv: wheat <- spelt and wheat <- meslin, both `defect`, no other product.

NOT A SUGAR CROP (data_errors.csv iia-other-sugar-crops-is-citrus). The raw IIA extract's only production-side products named `sugar` are bare `sugar`, `sugar: beet`, `sugar: cane` and `sugar: cane, unrefined`; no product could be an 'other sugar crop'. Value-matched on (year, value, area/production), the 62 dated rows read `citrus fruits: other` uniquely 23 times (algeria 5, australia 7, japan 6, zambia 5) and match a citrus product among several candidates 31 more times; the other 8, all italy, match nothing (4), one unrelated product (3: coffee, cottonseed, butter -- value collisions) or several non-citrus products (1). Both are residual 'other' buckets, which is how they were joined. A relabel to FAO `other citrus fruit, n.e.c.` is NOT applied: 31 of the citrus matches are ambiguous, italy's 14 rows cannot be attributed at all, and iia already carries a separate `other citrus fruit, n.e.c.` item. Shares no (polity, item, unit, year) key with another source, so withholding moves no mean; it stops publishing citrus as a sugar crop. state/item_equivalences.csv: other sugar crops n e c <- citrus fruits: other, `defect`, no other product.
